title: 2001 HMMT February Guts Problem 13
statement: Find the number of real zeros of \(x^{3}-x^{2}-x+2\).

solutions.text: Let \(f(x)=x^{3}-x^{2}-x+2\), so \(f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^{2}-2 x-1\). The slope is zero when \(3 x^{2}-2 x-1=0\), where \(x=-\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x=1\). Now \(f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)>0\) and \(f(1)>0\), so there are no zeros between \(x=-\frac{1}{3}\) and \(x=1\). Since \(\lim _{x \rightarrow+\infty} f(x)>0\), there are no zeros for \(x>1\). Since \(\lim _{x \rightarrow-\infty} f(x)<0\), there is one zero for \(x<-\frac{1}{3}\), for a total of 1 zero.
